newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise reports Norway drilling success.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise reports Norway drilling success.

text.p: Britain's Enterprise Oil on Wednesday announced a successful appraisal well, 30/5-2, drilled in the Norwegian part of the North Sea.
The well was drilled jointly by Royal Dutch/Shell Group, which has a 100 percent interest in block 30/5, and the block 30/8 group.

This group consists of Norway's Statoil with a 60 percent interest, Norsk Hydro ASA with 25 percent and Enterprise with 15 percent. "We are delighted with this successful appraisal of our 1995 discovery," said John Bullough, Enterprise's general Manager in Norway.

"(We) will be working closely with the PL 190 co-venturers in the coming months to evaluate options for further appraisal and/or development of this exciting addition to our Norwegian portfolio," said Bullough.
Well 30/5-2 encountered hydrocarbons in sediments of Jurassic age.
The best production test flowed 34.6 million cubic feet of gas per day and 3,208 barrels of oil/condensate per day.
The well was drilled as an appraisal of the 1995 discovery, 30/8-1S, which encountered hydrocarbons but was not tested due to operational restrictions on the licence.
